projects.name: 1.3.3.16 Sustainable Energy for Telefomin  - Papua New Guinea
projects.description:
The project’s main objectives are to develop practical and sustainable solutions to the provision of energy access in Telefomin, thereby introducing pathways between reliable electricity and development outcomes such as better incomes, health and increased education.

Aim of this project is to undertake a scoping exercise to assess local energy needs, including the installation of PV solar panels for five (5) buildings in Telefomin, the installation of a new transformer, and a thorough audit of buildings, fuses, switchboards, power lines and power poles. In addition the project intends to provide a framework for introducing an optimal set of technologies for the local mini-grid, leading to a gradual phase out of diesel fuel generation as the primary source of energy. 

The Project will be implemented in a phased approach, with clearly identified checkpoints at the end of each phase to facilitate a review of past actions and the validation of next phase actions and budgets.

This project falls under the Government-endorsed PNG Electrification Partnership (PEP), through which DFAT– alongside Japan, New Zealand and the United States – is supporting PNG to meet its target of electrifying 70 percent of the country by 2030.

projects.name: 1.3.3.13  Sustainable Energy for Baiyer - Papua New Guinea
projects.description:
The project’s main objectives are to develop practical and sustainable solutions to the provision of energy access in Mul-Baiyer  district (Baiyer River), thereby introducing pathways between reliable electricity and development outcomes such as better incomes, health and increased education.

The Bayer River solar project will assess the possibility of transitioning Mul-Baiyer  district to solar-hybrid energy solutions and offer practical steps to improve energy transmission and distribution infrastructure needs. Through this project UNOPS will conduct a detailed feasibility study for the electrification of Mul-Baiyer district. The study will cover the development of an independent hybrid mini-grid power system using solar PV and BESS (Battery energy storage system) with diesel generator backup. projects.name: Comprehensive Condom Program Situation Analysis
projects.description:
Background/Context:
In alignment with Government priorities for prevention of HIV and STI’s, Sexual Reproductive Health of Adolescent Youth and Family Planning, UNAIDS and UNFPA are supporting the development of a National Condom Programming Strategy in 2021 in partnership with the National Department of Health (NDoH) together with the National Aids Council Secretariat (NACS). 

Whilst significant progress has been made to improve access to HIV/AIDS and STIs services in many parts of the country over the recent years condom usage is still very low, especially among key populations and this continues to drive transmission of both HIV and STIs

The goal of condom programming is to ensure that sexually active persons including those at risk of HIV and STIs are motivated to use condoms, have easy access to quality condoms, and can use them consistently and correctly. In PNG this means all people are able to protect themselves, from STIs and HIV, and all people with STIs and HIV are able to access high-quality care, treatment and the support they need to maximize their health and the health of their families.

In alignment with the Government of PNG’s National STI and HIV Strategy 2018-2022 key strategic result area 3.0 Prevention and Continuum of Care, this means having the ‘right services, provided in the right places, accessed by the right people.’ The strategy importantly integrates key result areas that target prevention of and reduction in transmission of STI’s and HIV in both key/high risk populations and the general population. 

As such the first step in the development process is to undertake a comprehensive review of National Condom Programming in PNG. To do this we would like to coordinate and collaborate with the priority provinces of NCD, Morobe, Eastern Highlands and Western Highlands Provinces. This input together with contributions from relevant government of PNG departments, the identified key stakeholders from a range of sectors including civil society, local and International NGO’s, private sector supply and service providers and development partners, will ensure the review is inclusive and reflective of the diverse and collective experience of all.

National and provincial consultations, focus groups and interviews will be conducted in the provinces to better understand the experiences of successes, lessons learned and strategic priorities at a provincial level related to condom programming.

Results of the review will inform the revision and or development of the country’s future approach to National Comprehensive Condom Programming and the development of this will be aligned to Strategic Direction three under the current Papua New Guinea National STI and HIV Strategy 2018-2022.

projects.name: 4.1.2.9 - Enhancing political dialogue between the two Governments and the two Parliaments to ensure decisions around BPA implementation and referendum are progressed jointly
projects.description:
Progress on implementation of the BPA has been slow, but steady. A target date for the referendum was set for 15 June 2019, and the BRC was established. The successful conduct of the referendum, as enshrined in the BPA and in the Constitution of PNG, will be critical to finding a lasting and peaceful solution to the conflict in Bougainville, one that is accepted by both parties. The political relationship between the GoPNG and ABG is complex but encouraging. Testament to this is the successful JSB meeting held in December 2017 and October 2018 where key resolutions were made which significantly lowered political tensions over payments and other issues related to the conduct of the referendum including the Referendum Question. 

At this critical juncture of the peacebuilding process, as the referendum target date draws near, this activity will enable the UN to maintain its support to the Bougainville peace process, continuing with timely and coordinated technical and logistical assistance to the JSB, the Joint Technical Team (JTT), and both parliaments. Women’s participation in these meetings remains low, therefore this activity will try to ensure that women are actively engaged in the political decision-making and the political dialogue processes. This activity also includes support to monitoring of the implementation of the BPA by the two parliaments, including inter-parliamentary dialogue, as well as awareness and training on critical aspects of the Agreement. 

At the JSB meeting of May 2016, the two governments endorsed moving forward with a second joint review of Bougainville’s autonomy arrangements. Throughout the consultation process for this project, the two governments requested for the UN to assist in implementing such a review, which will be done through technical and financial support. This activity holds 50 per cent of the costs of the review, with the remainder supported by GoPNG and ABG. This represents a unique opportunity for the parties to work together to assess how Bougainville’s autonomy arrangements are progressing and constitutes a tool for both governments to improve the operation of the autonomy arrangements. 

This activity will be implemented in close partnership with the range of institutions, departments and other key actors working to advance the peace process in Bougainville. This will include, among others, the Offices of both Chief Secretaries, NCOBA, DPAI as well as both parliaments. 

Key outputs from this activity are:

(i)	JSB meets regularly and its resolutions are implemented jointly by the two governments;

(ii)	The two parliaments make joint decisions on the BPA and referendum processes, including on the post-referendum period in close consultations with women and youth focused civil society organizations;

(iii)	Key government institutions with responsibilities for BPA implementation and coordination between the two governments are enabled to implement their functions effectively.

Furthermore, agriculture activities such as; small livestock farming, apiculture, aquaculture and fresh food produce will be promoted and strengthened to address food and nutrition insecurity and for income generation. It is envisaged that this project will also help strengthen MSEs and SMEs, and contribute to the promotion of sustainable agricultural development within the target provinces. The project also focuses on the humanitarian-development nexus by implementing activities that address the immediate needs of target beneficiaries while making investments in building capacities to sustain activities beyond the life of the project

projects.name: 2.1.2.10 - Support green trade through non-tariff measures and voluntary sustainable standards and integrate green trade promotion into sustainable development strategies
projects.description: The project Green Trade for Sustainable Development in Pacific Small Island Developing States of the MSG is funded from the United Nations Development Account. It is implemented in close collaboration with the MSG secretariat. The project’s main objective is to increase the capacity of the government officials of the Melanesian Spearhead Group (MSG) countries - Fiji, Papua New Guinea, Vanuatu and Solomon Islands - to identify and strengthen synergistic linkages between green trade promotion and their sustainable development in a regionally collaborative manner. The project will support the target countries to achieve coherence and cross-feeding of policy actions by (1) increasing transparency of non-tariff measures (NTMs) through NTM data collection; (2) building capacity for sustainable trade through an assessment of the voluntary sustainable standards (VSS); and (3) developing synergistic linkages between the MSG member countries. The project's actual implementation was delayed to late 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

framework.name: Peace
framework.description:
Harnessing the UN's reputation as an impartial steward of Bougainville peace processes, the project aims to
support leaders, parliamentarians, officials and communities in PNG, and especially the Autonomous Region in Bougainville, to further
progress ongoing post-Referendum negotiations and related peace processes at the national and regional levels and to ensure that
diverse community members' voices are included in those processes. The project will also support a number of peace-supporting
economic development initiatives aimed at increasing opportunities for women and other marginalized groups to participate in the
formal economy, targeting those communities which had been particularly affected by the consequences of the Bougainville conflict
and in alignment with the existing Bougainville innovation hubs.
